Categories.value: Self-published work|Microscopic images of stems|Images from European Science Photo Competition 2015 in Russia|Microscopy images from European Science Photo Competition 2015|Featured pictures from Wiki Science Competition|Featured pictures of Ginkgoales|Featured pictures taken through a microscope|Microscopic images of Ginkgo|Uploaded via Campaign:espc-ru|Bright-field optical microscopic images

ImageDescription.value: Cross-section of the stem of a Gínkgo bilóba shoot (diameter: 4mm). Polychrome painting by Wacker. Stacking of 17 pictures. Brightfield. For this anatomical study, the shoot was taken from a plant that has been growing for many years in the greenhouse of the Omsk Children's Eco-Center. This plant species is often referred to as a "living fossil," as the Ginkgo group was widespread on Earth during the Mesozoic Era. The diameter of this cross-section of a *G. biloba* shoot is only 4 mm, and the thickness of the section is 30 micrometers. This photomicrograph is a composite (stitch) of 17 individual sectors of the cross-section. The preparation of the permanent slide, light microscopy, and bright-field illumination were performed by the author. Polychrome staining was applied using the Wacker method.

Artist.value: Anatoly Mikhaltsov
